description: List the passages elsewhere in the Bible most often linked to one verse, from the OpenBible.info cross-reference dataset (CC BY, stored locally), ranked by reader votes, strongest first, each read verbatim from the stored KJV. Use to follow a thread through Scripture ("verses related to Romans 8:28"). For the verses around a verse use scripture_context; for verses on a feeling use verses_for; for words in the text use scripture_search. Which passages are linked is a human judgement, labelled as such in content_layers. For a range in reference only its first verse is looked up; include_text false returns references and votes only (faster). A verse with no links returns count 0. Access: no sign-in; shared limit of 300 requests a minute per IP.

include_text.description: true (default): read each linked passage verbatim (up to 4 verses each, shortened flag set when cut). false: references and votes only.

reference.description: One verse: "Romans 8:28". For a range, its first verse is used; a whole chapter is an error.

name: cross_references

attribution.description: Credit line for the data: The Living Bread (living-bread.org).

content_layers.description: Marks Scripture fields and the human judgement of which passages link.

count.description: Linked passages returned; 0 when the verse has none.

evidence.description: Present when Scripture was read: translation, canon, corpus version, attribution, and a SHA-256 per passage.

freshness.description: How current the answer is: kind (scheduled | recently_observed | verified_live | record), retrieved_at, available_now (true only when activity was verified live).

ids.description: Up to 25 ids found in this answer, for follow-up calls.

next_actions.description: Up to 4 links the person can open next.

ok.description: Always true on a successful answer (errors come back as isError, never here).

references.description: Strongest first: reference, reader votes, verbatim KJV text (null when include_text is false), whether the text was shortened to 4 verses, and web link.

result_state.description: "empty" when nothing matched (count 0, no results); the text then says so plainly.

source_url.description: The first public web page this answer came from or points to.

visibility.description: "public" for shared data, "yours" for the signed-in believer's own data.

title: Cross references for a verse
